observations: White Xbox One S console with a physical disc slot.
One white Xbox wireless controller showing some surface dirt.
One blue Xbox wireless controller with visible wear on the thumbsticks.
Circular cooling vent on the top right of the console.
Watermark 'KINGSPLEN GAMING GADGETS' appears on all images.
The console appears to be the slim 'S' model, not the original bulky Xbox One or the All-Digital edition.

claims.evidence: External photos show wear on controllers; internal hardware state is unknown.
No games or digital content shown; 'FC 26' is not a released title (likely a typo for FC 24 or 25).

risks.proof: Screenshot of the 'Storage' section in System Settings.
Video of the console successfully loading and launching a game from a disc.

risks.risk: Controller stick drift or button failure
risks.proof: Video of both controllers being tested in the 'Xbox Accessories' app or a controller tester.

risks.risk: Console is banned from Xbox Live services
risks.proof: Video showing the console signed into a profile and accessing the Microsoft Store.

risks.risk: HDMI port or internal hardware failure
risks.proof: Video of the console booting up and displaying a stable image on a TV.

proof_requests: Video of the console booting up, reading a disc, and showing the storage capacity in settings.
Video of the console connected to the internet and signed into an Xbox account.
Clearer photos of the controller thumbsticks and buttons.
Clarification on the 'Fc26' claim as that game does not exist.
response.reason: The item is clearly an Xbox One S with two controllers. It can be priced at its worst-case scenario (500GB, non-functional disc drive, and no games) until further proof is provided.
